questions.stem: Two accessible subscriptions share a display name. What should CLZ-110 use to select the intended one?

options.A: The shared display name.
options.B: The first region shown.
options.C: The administrator's email alone.
options.D: Its exact subscription GUID.

optionExplanations.A: Names can collide and select the wrong context.
optionExplanations.B: Regions do not identify subscriptions.
optionExplanations.C: One identity can access multiple subscriptions.
optionExplanations.D: The ID avoids ambiguous display-name selection.

questions.stem: az login succeeds and lists several subscriptions. What remains necessary before later Terraform deployments?

options.A: Select and verify the intended subscription.
options.B: Create a VM to discover the subscription.
options.C: Register every resource provider.
options.D: Delete subscriptions you do not need.

optionExplanations.A: Authentication does not replace context verification.
optionExplanations.B: A read-only context query is sufficient.
optionExplanations.C: This lesson forbids provider registration.
optionExplanations.D: Access to other subscriptions does not justify deletion.

questions.stem: Which read-only command reports the currently selected tenant and subscription?

options.A: az account clear
options.B: az account show
options.C: az group create
options.D: terraform fmt

optionExplanations.A: That clears cached subscription information.
optionExplanations.B: Its result exposes the active account context.
optionExplanations.C: That creates a resource rather than reads context.
optionExplanations.D: Formatting cannot report Azure account metadata.

questions.stem: What does terraform apply tfplan do with the supplied CLZ-110 configuration?

options.A: Create a quota request automatically.
options.B: Register Microsoft.Compute.
options.C: Record local outputs without deploying Azure resources.
options.D: Create the first tagged resource group.

optionExplanations.A: Quota checks are explicit read-only CLI commands.
optionExplanations.B: The configuration does not perform provider registration.
optionExplanations.C: No resource or Azure provider is declared.
optionExplanations.D: That starts in CLZ-120.

questions.stem: A target VM family has zero remaining quota in eastus2. What is the appropriate next step?

options.A: Ignore quota because validate succeeded.
options.B: Change only the resource-group tag.
options.C: Attempt a larger size in the same constrained family.
options.D: Choose an approved alternative or request quota before deployment.

optionExplanations.A: Configuration validity does not create quota.
optionExplanations.B: Tags do not increase regional vCPU limits.
optionExplanations.C: That can worsen the shortage.
optionExplanations.D: Quota is a prerequisite to the later compute exercise.

questions.stem: Which CLZ-110 command inspects regional VM usage without requesting a quota change?

options.A: az vm list-usage --location eastus2
options.B: az vm create --location eastus2
options.C: az group delete --name quota
options.D: terraform destroy

optionExplanations.A: It reads usage and limits for the chosen region.
optionExplanations.B: VM creation is a deployment.
optionExplanations.C: Deleting a group is not a quota read.
optionExplanations.D: This is a state-driven deletion command.

questions.stem: A role appears on a different subscription from the intended lab. What should the learner conclude?

options.A: Any visible role applies to all subscriptions.
options.B: That assignment may not authorize the lab's target scope.
options.C: Logging in twice expands its scope.
options.D: A matching region name transfers permission.

optionExplanations.A: RBAC is scoped, not universal.
optionExplanations.B: RBAC permissions apply at their assigned scope and descendants.
optionExplanations.C: Authentication does not widen authorization.
optionExplanations.D: Region names do not transfer role assignments.

questions.stem: The user can sign in but cannot read required role information at the learning scope. What is the suitable response?

options.A: Self-assign Owner without approval.
options.B: Commit another user's access token.
options.C: Ask the subscription owner to review the needed access.
options.D: Remove all scope checks.

optionExplanations.A: The lesson does not authorize privilege elevation.
optionExplanations.B: Credentials must not be shared in the repository.
optionExplanations.C: Readiness should be resolved with an authorized scope owner.
optionExplanations.D: That hides the unresolved access problem.

questions.stem: The readiness command reads Microsoft.Compute registrationState. Which operation stays inside CLZ-110's read-only boundary?

options.A: az provider register --namespace Microsoft.Compute
options.B: terraform apply an Azure VM
options.C: az group create --name readiness
options.D: az provider show --namespace Microsoft.Compute

optionExplanations.A: Registration changes subscription configuration.
optionExplanations.B: The lesson's Terraform has no VM resource.
optionExplanations.C: Resource creation is outside this lesson.
optionExplanations.D: Show reads provider metadata without registering it.

questions.stem: Why inspect both tenantId and id in az account show?

options.A: They describe different identity and deployment boundaries.
options.B: The values must always be identical.
options.C: The tenant identifies the VM size.
options.D: The subscription identifies a single Azure region.

optionExplanations.A: A subscription ID is not a substitute for tenant context.
optionExplanations.B: They identify different Azure entities.
optionExplanations.C: A tenant is an identity directory, not compute sizing.
optionExplanations.D: A subscription can use multiple regions.

questions.stem: The selected subscription reports a state other than Enabled. What is the safe readiness decision?

options.A: Assume Terraform will enable it automatically.
options.B: Resolve the subscription state before proceeding.
options.C: Change the environment tag to prod.
options.D: Delete all local .tf files.

optionExplanations.A: Provider initialization does not repair subscription state.
optionExplanations.B: The expected usable context is Enabled.
optionExplanations.C: A tag does not enable billing or subscription access.
optionExplanations.D: That does not address subscription eligibility.

questions.stem: Which command changes the CLI's active subscription to the stored GUID?

options.A: az account show --subscription $env:ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID
options.B: terraform output subscription_id
options.C: az account set --subscription $env:ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID
options.D: az login --location eastus2

optionExplanations.A: Show is a read, not the documented context-selection step.
optionExplanations.B: Reading an output does not change Azure CLI context.
optionExplanations.C: Set selects the specified subscription context.
optionExplanations.D: A region is not a subscription selection argument.

questions.stem: CLZ-110 subscription_id is null. What does the generated subscription_source output indicate?

options.A: A new subscription has been created.
options.B: All accessible subscriptions will be changed.
options.C: The tenant ID is used as a subscription ID.
options.D: The readiness checks rely on active Azure CLI subscription context.

optionExplanations.A: The module declares no subscription resource.
optionExplanations.B: Its generated commands remain explicit reads.
optionExplanations.C: These identifiers have distinct meanings.
optionExplanations.D: The local configuration labels the source accordingly.

questions.stem: The readiness_commands output contains an az login string. Does displaying it log the learner in?

options.A: No; the learner must execute the command explicitly.
options.B: Yes, outputs execute each line automatically.
options.C: Only if the string contains a subscription ID.
options.D: Yes, but only in the Azure Portal.

optionExplanations.A: Terraform is emitting text, not invoking the Azure CLI.
optionExplanations.B: Output values are not shell execution hooks.
optionExplanations.C: Including an identifier does not execute text.
optionExplanations.D: The portal does not execute local Terraform outputs.

questions.stem: az account list-locations returns eastus2. What additional check is still needed for a planned Windows VM?

options.A: A new environment tag called eastus2.
options.B: The relevant VM-family quota and size availability.
options.C: A resource-group deletion test in every region.
options.D: A second copy of the README.

optionExplanations.A: A tag does not prove quota.
optionExplanations.B: Region listing alone is not a compute capacity guarantee.
optionExplanations.C: Destructive tests are not part of readiness.
optionExplanations.D: Duplicating documentation provides no capacity evidence.

questions.stem: A workstation runs Terraform but az is not recognized. What prerequisite is missing for CLZ-110's Azure checks?

options.A: An AzureRM resource block.
options.B: A VM public IP.
options.C: Azure CLI available on PATH.
options.D: A remote-state container.

optionExplanations.A: The readiness module intentionally has none.
optionExplanations.B: No VM is deployed here.
optionExplanations.C: The manual read-only commands require that executable.
optionExplanations.D: This lesson has no remote backend.

questions.stem: Which production onboarding choice matches the lesson's guidance?

options.A: Make every learner a permanent subscription Owner.
options.B: Share one personal token across the team.
options.C: Disable role review once login succeeds.
options.D: Use least-privilege groups and workload identities.

optionExplanations.A: That grants unnecessary authority.
optionExplanations.B: Shared personal credentials undermine accountability.
optionExplanations.C: Authentication does not establish appropriate scope.
optionExplanations.D: Avoid broad personal credentials for automation.

questions.stem: Why can CLZ-110's Terraform configuration be initialized before az login?

options.A: It declares no Azure provider or resources.
options.B: Terraform caches every Azure token in the source.
options.C: init creates an anonymous Azure subscription.
options.D: Quota information is baked into Terraform itself.

optionExplanations.A: The Azure checks are separate manually executed commands.
optionExplanations.B: The source does not contain such credentials.
optionExplanations.C: Initialization cannot provision an anonymous subscription.
optionExplanations.D: Live quota is queried through CLI reads.

questions.stem: What does Remove-Item Env:ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID remove in the documented cleanup?

options.A: The Azure subscription itself.
options.B: The current PowerShell process's environment variable.
options.C: Every RBAC role assigned to the user.
options.D: All Azure CLI authentication caches.

optionExplanations.A: Removing an environment variable does not delete a subscription.
optionExplanations.B: It clears the local selection input for later commands.
optionExplanations.C: RBAC assignments are separate Azure objects.
optionExplanations.D: The variable is not the complete CLI credential cache.

questions.learningObjective: Separate read-only actions from local settings
questions.stem: az account set changes the active CLI context. How should that action be classified?

options.A: A VM deployment in the selected region.
options.B: A role assignment that grants Contributor.
options.C: A local context selection without Azure resource deployment.
options.D: A backend migration.

optionExplanations.A: No VM is created.
optionExplanations.B: Context selection does not grant authorization.
optionExplanations.C: It affects subsequent command targeting, not resource provisioning.
optionExplanations.D: Terraform state is not moved by this CLI command.

questions.stem: CLZ-190 will use a particular VM family. Which quota row matters in CLZ-110?

options.A: Only the quota row for an unrelated region.
options.B: The number of resource-group tags.
options.C: The Terraform version number.
options.D: The corresponding family in the chosen region.

optionExplanations.A: Regional limits are independently relevant.
optionExplanations.B: Tags are not vCPU capacity.
optionExplanations.C: Terraform versions do not determine subscription quota.
optionExplanations.D: Family-specific regional limits can constrain deployment.

questions.learningObjective: Treat syntax checks as limited evidence
questions.stem: An optional subscription_id string passes the GUID validation. What has been proven?

options.A: The value matches the configured GUID format.
options.B: The user is Contributor on that subscription.
options.C: The subscription is Enabled.
options.D: The region has spare quota.

optionExplanations.A: The regex does not prove account access or subscription existence.
optionExplanations.B: Formatting is not an RBAC query.
optionExplanations.C: Only Azure context reads confirm its state.
optionExplanations.D: Quota is a different readiness check.

questions.stem: The exercise repeats readiness against a second subscription. Which comparison is most useful?

options.A: Only the README heading.
options.B: Subscription ID, tenant, role scope, and regional quota.
options.C: Only the subscription's display name.
options.D: Only the current local file size.

optionExplanations.A: The heading does not vary with account context.
optionExplanations.B: These facts determine deployment context and permissions.
optionExplanations.C: Names can repeat; IDs, tenant, scope, and quota provide stronger evidence.
optionExplanations.D: File size does not validate cloud context.

questions.stem: An account metadata query reports an expired authentication session. What is the appropriate repair?

options.A: Hardcode the expired token into Terraform.
options.B: Create an Azure resource to refresh the token.
options.C: Reauthenticate with az login and verify context again.
options.D: Disable all Azure permission checks.

optionExplanations.A: Expired credentials remain invalid and should not be committed.
optionExplanations.B: A deployment is unnecessary and may fail.
optionExplanations.C: Restoring a valid session does not remove the need to check the target.
optionExplanations.D: The authentication failure remains unresolved.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly relates Azure sign-in and resource creation permissions?

options.A: Every authenticated account has Owner.
options.B: Read permission automatically includes write permission.
options.C: Quota availability grants Contributor.
options.D: Successful authentication does not guarantee create permission.

optionExplanations.A: Login does not grant universal administration.
optionExplanations.B: Role actions distinguish reads and writes.
optionExplanations.C: Capacity and authorization are independent.
optionExplanations.D: RBAC must authorize the action at the target scope.

questions.stem: A learner remembers last week's selected subscription. What is the best evidence immediately before deployment?

options.A: A fresh az account show result checked against the intended GUID.
options.B: The name in an old CLI export.
options.C: The default environment=dev input.
options.D: The Terraform configuration's filename.

optionExplanations.A: Local context can change between sessions.
optionExplanations.B: An old export may not reflect current active context.
optionExplanations.C: Environment labels do not select subscriptions.
optionExplanations.D: The filename does not authenticate the account.

questions.stem: After CLZ-110, should the learner issue Azure deletions to remove its readiness reads?

options.A: Yes, delete the selected subscription.
options.B: No; the reads created no Azure resources.
options.C: Yes, delete every resource in eastus2.
options.D: Yes, revoke all roles shown.

optionExplanations.A: That is unrelated and destructive.
optionExplanations.B: Only local artifacts and configuration inputs need attention.
optionExplanations.C: Readiness queries do not establish ownership of those objects.
optionExplanations.D: Role reads do not create the assignments.

questions.stem: What prevents a Terraform-only CLZ-110 plan from creating an Azure VM?

options.A: A standard tag called ManagedBy.
options.B: The success of terraform validate alone.
options.C: The module contains no VM resource or Azure provider.
options.D: A special free Azure region.

optionExplanations.A: Metadata is not a global deployment block.
optionExplanations.B: Validation does not globally prevent cloud changes; this module's absence of resources does.
optionExplanations.C: Behavior follows actual configuration, not the lesson title.
optionExplanations.D: No region makes VM resources inherently nonexistent.

questions.stem: Why is CLZ-110 classified as having no deployed-resource cost?

options.A: Every Azure CLI command is always free of resource changes.
options.B: All Windows VMs are free during learning.
options.C: Tags automatically waive Azure billing.
options.D: It uses local outputs and read-only control-plane checks.

optionExplanations.A: CLI includes deployment and deletion commands too.
optionExplanations.B: Later Windows deployments incur costs.
optionExplanations.C: Tagging does not eliminate service charges.
optionExplanations.D: It provisions no VM, disk, gateway, or storage resource.

questions.stem: Which addition matches a production-ready process beyond the lab's basic reads?

options.A: Approved region, quota, policy, and budget review.
options.B: Skip checks when the account is an Owner.
options.C: Allow any region without organizational review.
options.D: Skip quota review for small VM sizes.

optionExplanations.A: The production delta adds governance around deployment readiness.
optionExplanations.B: High privilege does not remove cost or capacity constraints.
optionExplanations.C: The lesson calls for approved regions.
optionExplanations.D: Even small sizes can exceed regional family or total limits.
